name: request_revert
description: Ask the person to revert one change or one run of yours, or your own changes in one task you ran in: Basalt prepares the revert (as basalt revert does) and returns revertUrl, the page where the person reviews every row and signs with their passkey, and personMessage, the message to show the person verbatim, keeping its line breaks (put each link on a line of its own, exactly as given, or as [label](url) with the label from links). You can never sign a revert; you can only deliver the person's signature, which the database verifies. Before you call it, check the current data (preview_revert, and query for rows that depend on the change) and tell the person what you recommend. Name exactly one of changeId, runId, taskId, with intent (why the person reverts, in their words). Another agent's change or run, or a task you never ran in, is NOT_FOUND; a task revert holds only your own lines, and the person can include other agents' changes on the signing page. If another agent's run looks wrong, ask that agent. Show personMessage, then, without ending your turn, call request_revert once more with only revertId: that call waits up to waitForSignature seconds (default 90) and returns as soon as the person signs. APPLIED: the revert is done; tell the person what was restored and skipped. APPLYING (a revert over 1000 lines): the person signed the plan and you restore it now in batches (follow nextSteps). If the wait runs out (status PENDING), do not wait again: end your turn with the link and its expiry, and call request_revert with revertId when the person says they signed. If the person gives you a basalt-revert.1. code from the revert page, pass it as signature with revertId. People win: rows someone changed after you are skipped, never overwritten.

changeId.description: Revert one change (a revert's own changeId reverts that revert).

runId.description: Revert every applied change of one run.

taskId.description: Revert your own changes in one task you ran in (you have a run with that task id); only your own lines. The person can include other agents' changes on the signing page. A task you never ran in is NOT_FOUND.

runs.description: Only with taskId, 1 to 20 of your own runs with that task id; the revert holds only their lines and the page shows it as your proposal. Absent: all your runs in the task.

tables.description: With changeId, runId or taskId, 1 to 20 schema.table names, each a table you wrote in this scope; the revert holds only their lines. Absent: every table.

intent.description: Why the person reverts, in a sentence they can check on the revert page. Required with changeId, runId or taskId; refused with revertId.

revertId.description: A revert you requested: wait for the person's signature (or deliver it with signature) and return its state. Takes no scope and no intent.

waitForSignature.description: Only with revertId: seconds to wait for the person to sign before returning PENDING. Default 90; 0 returns the state at once.

reissueLink.description: Only with revertId, while PENDING: issue a new short link (the earlier one stops working) and return it as revertUrl. It returns at once, so the person gets the new link before you wait: not with waitForSignature or signature. Default false.

signature.description: Only with revertId: the basalt-revert.1. code the revert page showed the person, when they give it to you (the page could not relay it itself). The engine submits it and the database verifies the person's passkey signature, then applies the revert (a large plan: records the signature; you then apply it in batches). It must be for this revertId. It returns at once: not with waitForSignature. You cannot make one.

status.description: PENDING until the person signs; APPLIED once a revert of up to 1000 lines is signed (it is applied in the same transaction); APPLYING once a larger plan is signed and until you applied every line; EXPIRED when not signed within 1 hour, or a signed plan not finished within 24 hours. REJECTED when the person rejected it on the signing page; nothing was reverted, and you do not request it again unless the person asks.

scope.description: The scope you requested (TASK with taskId). Absent when widened (RS-5).

scopeId.description: The id you requested. Absent when widened (RS-5).

select.description: Planned (revert scope, RS-3): the scope descriptor of the revert as it stands, while the person has not widened it (your proposal, or the person's narrowing of it). Absent when widened: you cannot see what the person added.

widened.description: True when the person included other agents' changes. You then get only revertId, status, intent, batched, rows, skipped, expiresAt, personMessage and, for a large plan, changeId, applyBy and progress: no scope, select, lines or link. Absent or false otherwise.

rejectedAt.description: With REJECTED, when the person rejected it.

note.description: With REJECTED, the note the person wrote for you on the signing page, when they wrote one.

batched.description: True for a plan of more than 1000 lines: the person signs it once and you apply it with apply_revert_batch.

rows.description: Rows the signed revert restores (RESTORE lines).

skipped.description: Rows it leaves as they are because someone changed them after you (SKIP lines), as prepared.

expiresAt.description: The person must sign by then (1 hour after the request).

revertUrl.description: When the revert was just requested, or with reissueLink while PENDING: the revert page, the short link http://localhost:<port>/reverts/<revertId>#s=<secret> when the engine serves the local pages, else the long link <base>/reverts/<revertId>#1.<request>. Absent otherwise: the link already given keeps working.

personMessage.description: The message to show the person verbatim, keeping its line breaks: while PENDING what the revert restores and skips, the link on a line of its own (or a pointer to the link already given) and the expiry; otherwise the outcome.

links.description: The URLs of personMessage with labels, in order; present exactly when personMessage holds a URL.

changeId.description: Once APPLIED, or APPLYING: the revert's own change record (op REVERT), to show with run_history or revert with changeId.

applyBy.description: Batched plans, once signed: every line must be applied by then (24 hours after the signature).

progress.description: Batched plans, once signed: lines applied so far.

skipped.description: Lines skipped so far, at the signature and in batches.

nextSteps.description: What to do next, first step first (CONTRACT.md, Next steps): on PENDING the link for the person and the one wait; on PENDING after a wait, end your turn; on APPLYING the revert_plan and apply_revert_batch loop with arguments filled in; on EXPIRED, ask the person.
